summary: The pier light at the outer end of Grand Haven's north pier, lit by acetylene by 1915; the older light now stands at Coast Guard Park in Ferrysburg.

structures.note: Marks the outer end of the north pier (LighthouseFriends). Date of erection not established in the sources read.

Older 'Grand Haven North Pierhead (1?)' light, described as a white skeletal tower about 30 ft (9 m) tall; now at the entrance to Coast Guard Park, North Shore Drive, Ferrysburg (Lighthouse Directory). Date of removal unknown.

access.note: The Society's record says the north pier is not open to the public ('Open to Public: No'). WGHN reported in March 2026 that the north pier would be shut for up to two years from April 2026 for a Corps of Engineers project. Whether the light itself can be reached is not stated in the sources read.

events.note: Listed among aids in commission on 30 June 1915 using acetylene lights ('Grand Haven North Pierhead, Mich.').

Listed among lights whose illumination was improved in fiscal 1918, changed to electric incandescent ('Grand Haven Pierhead, Mich.'). The report does not name the pier; attribution to the north light is not confirmed.
North pier to be shut for up to two years from about April 2026 for an $8.25 million Corps of Engineers project (planned, per WGHN). The light itself is not mentioned.

corrections.why: The Lighthouse Directory lists 'Grand Haven North Pierhead (1?)' as the relocated, inactive skeletal light at Coast Guard Park. The active pier light is the D9 tower at the end of the pier.
A North Pierhead light was already listed in commission by 30 June 1915 (Commissioner's report). The sources read do not date the current D9 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station record gives 1921 (Wikidata, no references) as the build date. The Commissioner's 1915 report already lists a Grand Haven North Pierhead light in commission, so 1921 cannot be the date of the first light. It may be the date of the current tower, which the sources read do not date.

notes_for_editor: (1) THIN STATION. The sources read say little about this light's own history. The story is short and says so. (2) Identity: the station record's other name 'Grand Haven North Pierhead Light 1' belongs to the relocated, inactive skeletal light now at Coast Guard Park, Ferrysburg (Lighthouse Directory). The active record (Fl G 4s, 11 m, tower built 1921) describes the D9 pier light. Decide whether the 'Light 1' name should move. (3) The 1921 build date is from Wikidata with no references (search snippet only; the entity was not fetched). The 1915 report already lists the light, so 1921 is at most the current tower's date. (4) Fiscal 1918 entry: 'Grand Haven Pierhead, Mich.' is ambiguous. Grand Haven has pierhead lights on both piers, and the report names no pier for that row. The story does not tie it to the north light. (5) Ownership: the story does not state an owner. The agency field was removed because no source read names the owner of the north light. LighthouseFriends and the directory give city ownership for the south pierhead lights. (6) LighthouseFriends' pier-light history (the 1883 and 1885 extensions, the 1886 gale, the 1905 metal tower on the south pier, the 1961 rescue at the end of the south pier) is not tied to the north pierhead tower in the sources read, so it is not used. The Pendergrast passage (1837) is used only for the river and its bar. The Grand Haven South/Range keeper rosters (USLHS 'Grand Haven South Pierhead Range', 97 lines) belong to other stations and are not used. (7) Not verified: whether the North light was ever staffed, and when the D9 tower replaced the older light. The ibiblio entry says 'Date unknown.' (8) A Saugatuck pierhead entry on the same ibiblio page (north pierhead established 1914, focal plane 30 ft) is a different station and was not used. (9) The 1915 and 1918 Commissioner entries were read from the page OCR (the 1915 list is a run of names under the acetylene heading; the 1918 row sits under the third category heading). The page image was not viewed. Check the scan before reprinting the lists.
